  "title": "AffordInvar: Self-Supervised Spatial Affordance Learning in VLAs via Instruction Invariance and Cross-Object Transfer",
  "core_problem": "Can we learn explicit spatial affordance representations within an end-to-end Vision-Language-Action model without any affordance annotations, by jointly exploiting (1) instruction paraphrase invariance — semantically equivalent instructions must activate identical spatial affordance regions — and (2) cross-object affordance transfer — objects with similar functional parts must exhibit similar affordance patterns for the same interaction type — producing interpretable intermediate representations that improve manipulation success, paraphrase robustness, and zero-shot generalization to novel objects beyond what action-level invariance methods (RSS, LangForce) or standalone affordance modules (INTRA, AffordanceSAM) can achieve?",
  "opportunity": "LIBERO-Para (arXiv 2603.28301, March 2026) reveals that VLAs suffer 22-52 percentage point drops under simple paraphrasing, with 80-96% of failures at the planning level — confirming that VLAs rely on surface-level instruction matching rather than semantic grounding. RSS (arXiv 2601.04052, January 2026) addresses this at the action level via Residual Affordance Steering, achieving strong results on π₀/π₀.₅, but operates only on final-layer logits without learning spatial affordance structure — missing richer intermediate signals. INTRA (ECCV 2024) demonstrates that text synonym augmentation with contrastive learning produces effective affordance maps on AGD20K, but remains a standalone perception module disconnected from robot action prediction. No method bridges spatial affordance learning and VLA action prediction in an end-to-end self-supervised manner. Meanwhile, the context-dependent affordance study (arXiv 2603.04419) reveals that while VLM-computed affordances show >90% lexical drift across contexts, stable latent affordance factors persist — suggesting that spatial affordance structure is invariant under linguistic variation and exploitable as self-supervision.   "landscape": "RSS (arXiv 2601.04052, January 2026) uses Monte Carlo Syntactic Integration (LLM-generated paraphrases averaged over K variations) and Residual Affordance Steering (subtracting vision-only prior from language-conditioned prediction at the action logit level) to achieve 82.2% on π₀ (vs 52.4% baseline) and 90.0% on LIBERO-Plus — the closest methodological precedent, but explicitly operates at the action output level with no learned spatial affordance maps, limiting interpretability and structured transfer. INTRA (ECCV 2024, arXiv 2409.06210) uses ChatGPT-4-generated synonyms with interaction-relationship-guided contrastive learning for text-conditioned affordance map generation, achieving SOTA on AGD20K/UMD — directly anticipates paraphrase-invariance for affordance, but is a standalone perception module not integrated into VLA action prediction. WSAG-PLSP (ICLR 2025) uses part-level semantic priors from foundation models for weakly supervised affordance grounding with breakthrough results — standalone, requires pseudo-label generation pipeline. AffordanceSAM (April 2025) extends SAM to affordance grounding via coarse-to-fine training, achieving current SOTA on AGD20K — supervised, standalone. BiT-Align (IROS 2025) achieves 6% KLD improvement on AGD20K with 88.8% fewer parameters via depth+semantic prompts — efficient but standalone. LIBERO-Para (arXiv 2603.28301, March 2026) is a diagnostic benchmark revealing 22-52pp VLA performance drops under paraphrasing with the PRIDE metric — confirms the problem but proposes no solution. SelfEQ (CVPR 2024) demonstrates LLM-paraphrase self-consistency loss improves VLM grounding on ReferIt/Flickr30K — methodological inspiration for paraphrase invariance, but applied to general visual grounding, not affordance or robot manipulation. CoA-VLA (ICCV 2025) integrates chain-of-affordance reasoning into VLAs with supervised affordance labels, outperforming OpenVLA and Octo — demonstrates affordance-action integration value but requires annotation. GeneralVLA (arXiv 2602.04315, February 2026) proposes a hierarchical VLA with an external Affordance Segmentation Module for zero-shot 3D trajectory planning, outperforming VoxPoser — but the affordance module is externally supervised, not self-supervised within the VLA. RT-Affordance (ICRA 2025) uses affordances as intermediate representations achieving 69% vs 15% for language-conditioned baselines — two-stage pipeline with supervised affordance learning. RobustVLA (ICLR 2026) enforces action-level consistency under 17 perturbation types — action-level, not intermediate representations. Synthetic instruction augmentation for OpenVLA (arXiv 2603.16044, March 2026) uses LLM paraphrases as LoRA fine-tuning data — treats paraphrases as supervised examples, not self-supervised consistency signal. VoxPoser (CoRL 2023) composes 3D value maps from LLMs for zero-shot manipulation — no learned affordance representations, relies on LLM code generation at inference time. OVAL-Prompt (2024) achieves open-vocabulary affordance localization via VLM+LLM prompting without fine-tuning — competitive zero-shot baseline but not an integrated VLA. The critical gap: no work learns explicit spatial affordance maps within an end-to-end VLA via self-supervision — RSS/LangForce operate at the action level, INTRA/AffordanceSAM/WSAG-PLSP are standalone perception modules, and CoA-VLA/RT-Affordance/GeneralVLA use supervised affordance labels or external modules.",
  "approach": "We propose AffordInvar, which augments OpenVLA-OFT with a lightweight spatial affordance decoder and trains it jointly with the VLA via LoRA using two complementary self-supervised signals: instruction paraphrase invariance and cross-object affordance transfer. **Architecture**: The affordance decoder takes intermediate features from the VLA's 18th transformer layer (out of 32), which retain spatial structure before the final action-prediction layers. The decoder consists of 3 transposed convolution blocks (each: ConvTranspose2d 4×4 stride 2, GroupNorm, GELU) upsampling from 16×16 to 128×128 resolution, with text conditioning via the instruction embedding projected through a linear layer and channel-wise multiplied at each block (~8M parameters total, <0.12% of VLA backbone). Output is a sigmoid-activated 128×128 affordance heatmap. **Self-supervised signal 1 — Paraphrase invariance (L_consist)**: For each training episode, Qwen 3 generates K=3 semantically equivalent instruction paraphrases offline. During training, each paraphrase-image pair is processed through the VLA, and a symmetric KL divergence loss enforces identical affordance heatmaps across all K+1 instruction variants: L_consist = (1/C(K+1,2)) Σ_{i<j} KL(h_i || h_j), extending SelfEQ's visual grounding consistency (CVPR 2024) from general VLM grounding to the VLA affordance domain. Unlike RSS which applies paraphrase averaging at the action logit level, we enforce consistency at the intermediate spatial representation level, providing richer structured learning signal. **Self-supervised signal 2 — Cross-object affordance transfer (L_transfer)**: Episodes with semantically similar instructions (cosine similarity > 0.85 on instruction embeddings) but different target objects are mined as positive pairs; episodes with the same object but different interaction types serve as negatives. A contrastive InfoNCE loss on spatially-normalized affordance features encourages interaction-specific (not object-specific) affordance representations, enabling zero-shot transfer to novel objects — inspired by INTRA's interaction-relationship contrastive learning but operating on VLA-internal features with free-form instructions rather than predefined interaction labels. **Affordance-action integration**: The affordance heatmap is bilinearly downsampled to the action feature resolution and applied as an element-wise gate: action_features = action_features ⊙ σ(W_g · affordance_features + b_g), where W_g is a learned linear projection (~0.5M parameters). This is more parameter-efficient than cross-attention while still allowing affordance-guided action prediction. **Entropy regularization**: To prevent degenerate uniform or collapsed heatmaps, we add H_entropy = -λ_H Σ h_i log(h_i), encouraging peaked but non-trivial affordance predictions. **Total loss**: L = L_action + α·L_consist + β·L_transfer + λ_H·H_entropy, where L_action is OpenVLA-OFT's continuous L1 action regression loss. **Evaluation**: (1) Manipulation success on LIBERO-Long (10 tasks, standard) and LIBERO-Para (paraphrase robustness, measuring PRIDE score); (2) Zero-shot generalization to held-out object categories within LIBERO; (3) Affordance localization quality evaluated zero-shot on AGD20K and UMD (the affordance decoder applied to these benchmarks without fine-tuning, testing whether VLA-learned affordance representations transfer to standard affordance benchmarks); (4) Qualitative affordance map visualization and contact-point prediction accuracy on held-out LIBERO episodes. **Baselines**: OpenVLA-OFT (vanilla, no affordance), OpenVLA-OFT + RSS-style action-level paraphrase invariance (our reimplementation), INTRA affordance maps + OpenVLA-OFT policy (two-stage), CoA-VLA, GeneralVLA, VoxPoser, OVAL-Prompt + learned policy. **Key hypotheses**: (a) Spatial affordance consistency provides better paraphrase robustness than action-level consistency (RSS) because it prevents shortcut learning at a more fundamental representation level; (b) Cross-object affordance transfer enables superior zero-shot generalization to novel objects compared to methods without explicit affordance structure; (c) Self-supervised affordance representations learned within a VLA can transfer zero-shot to standard affordance benchmarks, demonstrating genuine affordance understanding rather than task-specific memorization.",

## Reviewer feedback (round 2)
Issues: ["CRITICAL MISSING RELATED WORK: SP-VLA/ST4VLA (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2602.10109) uses spatial priors (point, box, trajectory predictions) to guide VLA action generation end-to-end, trained on web-scale grounding data (RefCOCO etc.), and explicitly claims 'stronger generalization to unseen objects and paraphrased instructions.' Achieves 62% zero-shot on unseen objects vs. 32% for π₀. This is the closest concurrent work occupying the 'spatial representations within end-to-end VLA' space. While SP-VLA uses supervised spatial grounding rather than self-supervised affordance maps, the overlapping claims (spatial guidance → paraphrase robustness + novel object generalization) demand explicit comparison and differentiation.", "MISSING RELATED WORK: PALM (arXiv 2601.07060, January 2026) learns structured affordance representations (object relevance, contact geometry, spatial placements, motion dynamics) within an end-to-end VLA, achieving 91.8% on LIBERO-Long. Uses supervised semi-automated annotation. Directly relevant as another 'affordance within VLA' approach.", "MISSING RELATED WORK: SG-VLA (arXiv 2603.22760, March 2026) co-trains auxiliary affordance decoders with VLA backbone using dense supervision, reconstructing grasp affordances, segmentation masks, and other intermediate signals from shared visual-language features. Another concurrent 'affordance decoder in VLA' approach.", "OVER-OPTIMISTIC ZERO-SHOT AGD20K/UMD EVALUATION: The proposal claims VLA-learned affordance representations will 'transfer zero-shot to standard affordance benchmarks (AGD20K, UMD).' The domain gap between LIBERO simulation images (rendered robot workspace scenes) and AGD20K/UMD images (real-world exocentric human-object interactions and egocentric object images) is enormous. This evaluation is likely to produce poor results and weaken rather than strengthen the paper. At minimum, acknowledge this gap explicitly and frame it as 'preliminary/exploratory evaluation' rather than a core contribution.", "SCOPE NARROWING FROM SEED: The seed explicitly asks for 'open-vocabulary affordance zero-shot VLA' handling instructions like 'use this thing to wipe off the dust over there.' The proposal's paraphrase invariance addresses instruction surface form robustness (different phrasings of the same instruction), not truly open-vocabulary novel interaction types (e.g., training on 'pick up' and generalizing to 'scoop out'). The cross-object transfer component partially addresses this but the free-form novel interaction instruction tests (required by the seed) are not clearly specified in the evaluation protocol.", "SELF-SUPERVISED SIGNAL QUALITY RISK NOT ADDRESSED: The core claim that paraphrase invariance produces meaningful spatial affordance heatmaps (not just blurry attention blobs) is the key technical bet. The proposal mentions entropy regularization to prevent degenerate solutions but doesn't discuss: (a) what happens if paraphrases only differ in action verbs but not spatial referents — the affordance map may correctly be identical, providing no learning signal about WHERE to attend; (b) how the contrastive cross-object transfer loss interacts with the invariance loss — could they conflict?"]
Feedback: The revision has substantially improved from Round 1 — RSS/INTRA/LangForce are now properly cited, compute is within budget, architecture is detailed, and baselines are comprehensive. Three targeted fixes to push toward pass:

1. **Cite and differentiate from SP-VLA (ICLR 2026), PALM (Jan 2026), and SG-VLA (Mar 2026)**: These are the three most relevant concurrent works that the proposal misses. SP-VLA is the most critical — it already shows spatial priors in VLA → better paraphrase robustness + novel object generalization (supervised). Your key differentiation: (a) self-supervised vs. supervised — your method requires no spatial annotations, making it applicable to any VLA dataset; (b) affordance heatmaps vs. point/box/trajectory — your representation captures continuous interaction regions rather than discrete points; (c) the paraphrase invariance signal is theoretically grounded in the observation (from LIBERO-Para) that VLA failures are at the planning level, suggesting intermediate representation consistency is more important than action-level or explicit spatial supervision.

2. **Soften or restructure AGD20K/UMD evaluation**: Either (a) acknowledge the domain gap and frame zero-shot affordance benchmarking as 'exploratory/secondary evaluation' rather than a core claim, or (b) add a fine-tuning/adaptation step where you fine-tune only the affordance decoder on AGD20K training data while freezing VLA backbone — this would test whether VLA-learned affordance representations provide useful initialization. Option (b) is actually a stronger experiment that tests representation quality rather than zero-shot transfer across wildly different domains.

3. **Strengthen the open-vocabulary / novel interaction evaluation**: Add a specific evaluation protocol for the seed's requirement of 'novel interaction instruction generalization.' For example: hold out entire interaction types from LIBERO training (e.g., all 'opening' tasks) and test whether affordance maps generalize to these unseen interactions. Also add 'free-form instruction tests' — Qwen 3 can generate creative rephrasings that describe the same task using novel interaction vocabulary (e.g., 'unfasten the container' instead of 'open the drawer'). This directly addresses the seed's concern about open-vocabulary capability.

Minor: Consider ICRA 2027 as co-primary target alongside AAAI 2027, since the contribution is more naturally a robotics contribution than an AI-general one.

## 深度调研要求（每一轮修订都必须执行）

不要简单地'打补丁'——每一轮修订都是重新审视和深化这个 idea 的机会。

1. **深度搜索**：针对 reviewer 指出的每个问题，建议用 2-3 种不同的搜索查询调研。
   - 搜索最新的相关论文（arXiv, conference proceedings）
   - 搜索 benchmark/leaderboard 确认当前 SOTA
   - 搜索可能遗漏的相关工作和 concurrent work

2. **深度阅读**：用 WebFetch 实际阅读找到的关键论文的 abstract 和方法部分，
   不要只依赖搜索摘要。形成你自己对领域现状的独立判断。

3. **深度思考**：在修订之前，先独立思考以下问题：
   - 这个 idea 的核心假设是否仍然成立？
   - reviewer 的批评是否揭示了更深层的问题？
   - 有没有更好的 framing 或 approach 来解决同一个核心问题？
   - 修订后的 idea 相比上一版有什么本质性的改进？

4. **避免表面修订**：如果你发现自己只是在换措辞或补充细节而没有实质改进，
   考虑是否需要 major revision 或 pivot。反复的 minor fix 不会拯救一个根基有问题的 idea。

## 针对 Review 意见的定向搜索

对 reviewer 指出的每个问题，执行以下搜索流程：

1. **如果 reviewer 说'已有类似工作'**：
   - 搜索 reviewer 提到的论文，用 WebFetch 实际阅读
   - 搜索该论文的 cited-by，找到后续跟进工作
   - 明确你的 idea 与这些工作的差异化点——如果差异化不够，必须 pivot

2. **如果 reviewer 说'SOTA 过时'**：
   - 用 Papers With Code 查看当前排行榜
   - 搜索过去 6 个月的最新方法
   - 更新你的 landscape 和 baseline

3. **如果 reviewer 说'可行性有问题'**：
   - 搜索类似规模实验的实际成本和时间线
   - 搜索 GitHub 上是否有可复用的实现
   - 搜索相关数据集/模型的可获取性

4. **如果 reviewer 说'novelty 不足'**：
   - 对核心方法尽量做 3-5 种不同关键词组合的搜索
   - 搜索相邻领域是否有类似思路
   - 如果确实 novelty 不足，考虑 major revision 或 pivot

- Use WebSearch to find updated information if the reviewer flagged outdated claims.
- You have full freedom in how much to change:
  - Minor fix: if only specific details are wrong, correct them and keep everything else.
  - Major revision: if the approach is fundamentally flawed but the core problem is valid, you may redesign the approach entirely.
  - Pivot: if the reviewer's feedback reveals that the core problem itself is invalid (e.g., the gap no longer exists), you may propose a RELATED but substantially different idea that builds on the same research area. This is preferred over forcing a doomed idea to pass review.

# SG-VLA Paper Summary

## Full Abstract
"Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models show promise for robotic control, yet performance in complex household environments remains sub-optimal. Mobile manipulation requires reasoning about global scene layout, fine-grained geometry, and high-dimensional continuous actions, making standard imitation learning insufficient. We introduce a framework for learning spatially-grounded VLA models that strengthens perception and representation through auxiliary task co-training and multi-modal input enhancement. Our method addresses the challenge of controlling a 13-dimensional action space involving coordinated base motion, arm articulation, and gripper actuation. To enrich spatial understanding, the model incorporates multi-view RGB observations, depth cues, and short temporal history, providing perspectives of both global scene structure and local manipulation context. To improve representation quality, we co-train auxiliary decoders that reconstruct interpretable intermediate signals - including global robot position, joint configurations, grasp affordances, target-object relative pose, and segmentation masks - from shared visual-language features. These objectives provide dense supervision that encourages the backbone to develop spatially grounded, manipulation-aware latent representations. Through extensive evaluation on home rearrangement tasks, our approach achieves consistent improvements across picking, placing, opening, and closing operations, substantially outperforming direct imitation learning. Our findings suggest that spatial grounding through auxiliary and multi-modal learning provides a strong direction for scaling VLA models toward general-purpose domestic robots."

## Key Method Details

**Auxiliary Decoders & Supervision:**
The framework co-trains five auxiliary decoders that reconstruct: global robot position, joint configurations, grasp affordances, target-object relative pose, and segmentation masks. # ST4VLA: Detailed Method and Experimental Analysis

## Spatial Priors Predicted

ST4VLA predicts three types of spatial outputs: **point predictions** (object localization), **bounding boxes** (object detection), and **trajectory predictions** (action paths). These are learned during the first stage and leveraged to guide action generation in stage two.

## Web-Scale Data for Spatial Grounding Pre-training

The model combines internet-scale datasets with robot-specific data:
- **General datasets**: RefCOCO, LLaVA-OneVision
- **Robot-specific datasets**: RoboRefIt, A0, ST4VLA Data

"This combination ensures that the VLM's spatial priors are not only grounded in broad visual concepts but are also directly relevant to robotic tasks" (Section 2.2).

## Spatial Prompting in Stage 2

During action post-training, spatial prompts are appended to task instructions to activate spatial reasoning. For example: "Identify all relevant toys and their spatial relationships to the container" augments "store all toys into the toy box." The VLM planner generates latent spatial embeddings conditioning the DiT action expert through a lightweight querying transformer (8.7 MB) with gradient decay (0.5 factor) to preserve semantic knowledge.

## LIBERO Results

ST4VLA achieves 95.9% average success across LIBERO benchmarks:
- Spatial: 98.0%
- Objects: 99.0%
- Goal: 93.8%
- Long: 92.6%

This outperforms baselines like π₀ (94.2%) and GR00T N1 (93.9%).

## Zero-Shot Unseen Object Generalization

On real-world pick-and-place with new instances, ST4VLA achieves **62% success** versus π₀'s 32% and GR00T's 46%—substantially demonstrating generalization to novel objects.

## Paraphrase Robustness

Under "unseen instructions" with paraphrased commands, ST4VLA reaches **52% success**, compared to π₀'s 18% and GR00T's 20%, demonstrating strong linguistic robustness.

## Training Parameters and Compute Requirements

The document does not specify total training parameters or computational requirements (GPU hours, memory). It mentions "8 A100 GPUs with batch size 128" for LIBERO fine-tuning lasting "about 20 hours," but comprehensive compute metrics for the full pipeline are absent.

# PALM: Detailed Method Analysis

## 1. Four Affordance Representations: Generation Method

The affordances are **semi-automatically generated with human annotation** during fine-tuning:

- **Global & Local**: Derived using external tools. Global affordances employ "Grounding DINO...and then segmenting the instance with SAM" to obtain object masks and features.

- **Spatial**: Generated via "SpatialVLM...and then sampling executable 2D coordinates with RoboPoint."

- **Dynamic**: Constructed through "grid-based tracking protocol" where "CoTracker follows each point forward in time" to identify moving regions.

The paper states: "For fine-tuning, we select 942 trajectories from robot data and annotate them with affordance data and continuous progress labels using a semi-automated method."

## 2. Affordance Prediction Module Architecture

PALM uses **four specialized decoder heads** attached to the backbone:

## Affordance Field Intervention (AFI): Enabling VLAs to Escape Memory Traps

Affordance Field Intervention (AFI) is a lightweight hybrid framework that uses Spatial Affordance Fields (SAFs) as an on-demand plugin to guide VLA behavior.

### The Problem: Memory Traps

Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models remain brittle under distribution shifts: when test scenarios change, VLAs often reproduce memorized trajectories instead of adapting to the updated scene, a failure mode referred to as the "Memory Trap". This limitation stems from the end-to-end design, which lacks explicit 3D spatial reasoning and prevents reliable identification of actionable regions in unfamiliar environments.

### The Solution

3D Spatial Affordance Fields (SAFs) provide a geometric representation that highlights where interactions are physically feasible, offering explicit cues about regions the robot should approach or avoid. The system detects memory traps through proprioception, repositions the robot to recent high-affordance regions, and proposes affordance-driven waypoints that anchor VLA-generated actions, with a SAF-based scorer then selecting trajectories with the highest cumulative affordance.

### Results

The method achieves an average improvement of 23.5% across different VLA backbones under out-of-distribution scenarios on real-world robotic platforms, and 20.2% on the LIBERO-Pro benchmark.

**Summary of changes (minor revision):**

1. **ST4VLA/PALM/SG-VLA/Spatial Forcing/AFI integrated throughout**: All five concurrent works now appear in the landscape, opportunity, approach, and references. The differentiation is clear and substantive: all use supervised/semi-supervised signals (web-scale grounding data, annotation pipelines, pretrained 3D models), while AffordInvar requires zero spatial annotations. ST4VLA's strong numbers (95.9% LIBERO, 62% zero-shot) actually *validate* the spatial-representations-in-VLA thesis — we now frame this as "the value is confirmed, but can we get there without annotation?"

2. **AGD20K evaluation restructured**: Primary evaluation is now decoder fine-tuning with frozen VLA backbone (tests representation quality as initialization), with zero-shot transfer explicitly downgraded to "secondary/exploratory" with honest acknowledgment of the simulation-to-real domain gap. UMD dropped to simplify.

3. **Novel interaction evaluation added**: Held-out entire interaction types from LIBERO training (e.g., all 'opening' or 'stacking' tasks), tested with Qwen-3-generated creative rephrasings using novel vocabulary ('unfasten the container' for 'open the drawer'). This directly addresses the seed's open-vocabulary requirement.

4. **Signal quality concerns addressed**: Explicit analysis of verb-only paraphrases (correctly produce identical maps — valid signal for linguistic invariance, but insufficient alone for spatial grounding), and why L_consist and L_transfer are complementary rather than conflicting (distinct roles: linguistic invariance vs. functional grounding, with mining procedure preventing contradictory targets). Added effective-pixel diagnostic (exp(entropy)/total_pixels) with concrete thresholds for automated collapse/diffuse detection.

5. **Venue targeting adjusted**: ICRA 2027 elevated to co-primary alongside AAAI 2027, per reviewer's suggestion that this is more naturally a robotics contribution.

6. **Hypothesis (c) softened**: Now frames self-supervised approach as "approaching" supervised performance while being annotation-free, rather than claiming superiority — a more honest and defensible position.
